choices: Priya, the regular who never loses

floor.name: Arcade floor
floor.text: Two in the morning at the Starlight Arcade. The cabinets are still on, each one running its attract screen for nobody, and their glow puts long colored shadows across the carpet you were hired to vacuum. A Block Drop cabinet stands by the front window. Beside it is a square of carpet that is cleaner than the rest, where a cabinet used to be. Your mop and bucket wait by the door to the prize counter, and a doorway at the back of the floor leads west into the staff hallway.

extra.text: The Block Drop cabinet is sulking in service mode.

counter.name: Prize counter
counter.text: The prize counter. Shelves of plush bears and plastic sunglasses stand behind a steel grille, with the stockroom door somewhere behind them, and a slush machine churns a blue drink that nobody has bought since summer. Behind the counter, three staff lockers lean against the wall, and a pickup ledger lies open beside the register.

extra.text: The grille is rolled down and padlocked at the floor.
The grille is rolled up far enough to duck under; the stockroom is in.

exits.name: the stockroom behind the grille
exits.fail: The steel grille is padlocked at the floor. The stockroom is behind it.

office.name: Back office
office.text: A back office the size of a closet: a desk with a chair, a floor safe under it, and a panel of little keyed switches on the wall, one per cabinet. The desk lamp is on. Marge, who owns the place, is doing the books at two in the morning and does not look surprised to see you.

extra.text: The safe hangs open under the desk.

hallway.name: Back hallway
hallway.text: A narrow staff hallway behind the arcade floor, lit by one fluorescent tube that cannot decide whether to stay on. A fuse box hangs open on the wall beside a faded Galaxy Patrol poster. A steel door at the north end leads to the loading dock, and a stairwell goes down to the basement workshop. The arcade floor is back east.

dock.name: Loading dock
dock.text: The loading dock: a concrete platform under one caged bulb, with the roll-up door standing open on the alley and the night air coming in. A hand dolly leans against the wall. A clipboard hangs from a nail by the door, and a lift lever juts from a box on the wall above a painted warning. Fresh tyre tracks curve away from the platform into the dark.

alley.name: Alley
alley.text: The alley behind the Starlight, wet asphalt shining under a sodium lamp. A delivery van with the distributor's name on the side is parked nose-out. A payphone hangs on the arcade's wall beside a dumpster, and an oil stain spreads where something heavy sat for a while. The diner's back door is west, under a buzzing sign; the dock is back in through the roll-up door.

extra.text: The van's back doors are shut.
The van's back doors stand open.

van.name: Inside the van
van.text: The cargo bay of the delivery van. It smells of rubber and cold coffee. Something tall and square stands strapped against the bulkhead under a pile of moving blankets, and a shipping label is taped to the strap.

diner.name: Starlight Diner, back counter
diner.text: The back counter of the Starlight Diner, open all night and nearly empty. Coffee pots sit on their burners under a pie case with two slices left. Lou, the night cook, leans on the counter with a crossword. On the last stool, a man in a distributor's jacket is asleep with his head on his arms. The arcade's alley is out the back door east.

workshop.name: Basement workshop
workshop.text: Rudy's workshop, in the basement under the floor: a long bench under a hanging lamp, a parts cabinet with three drawers, a toolbox, and a monitor chassis lying open on the bench with its back off and a yellow warning sticker on the frame. A soldering iron rests in its stand, still warm. The smell of flux is everywhere. The stairs go back up to the hallway.

stockroom.name: Stockroom
stockroom.text: The stockroom behind the prize counter: steel shelves of plush animals in plastic bags, boxes of tokens, a stack of flattened cartons. Leaning against the back wall is a sheet of painted plywood with a jigsaw's ragged edge: the back panel of an arcade cabinet, sawn off. Sawdust is everywhere. The way out is through the grille.

cabinet.name: Block Drop cabinet
cabinet.text: A Block Drop cabinet, the arcade's pride, with a coin slot, a joystick worn smooth, and the high score board glowing above the screen. The attract screen drops blocks for no one. The gap under the cabinet is too low for a hand.

extra.text: Something small catches the light in the dust under there.
There is nothing under it now but dust and a bottle cap.
The screen is stuck on its service page.

board.name: high score board
board.text: The high score board lists ten names. The top one is new: ZZZ, 999,999 points, entered at 3:07 this morning. Nobody was playing at 3:07; you locked the doors at midnight. Below it, the honest scores, the best of them by someone who signs as PRI.

gap.name: clean square of carpet
gap.text: A rectangle of carpet, cleaner and darker than the rest, with four dents where the feet of a cabinet stood for years. A power cord trails from the wall into the space and ends in nothing. The ledger at the prize counter would say what left and when.

mop.name: mop
mop.text: A string mop, mostly gray. It came with the job.

bucket.name: bucket
bucket.text: A yellow bucket on wheels, half full of water that was clean once.

cord.name: frayed power cord
cord.text: The power cord that fed the missing cabinet. It trails from the wall into the clean square of carpet, and the insulation near the plug is split open to the copper.

token.name: arcade token
token.text: A brass Starlight token, good for one play.

door.name: office door
door.text: A plain door with OFFICE stenciled on it and a brass lock that the owner is particular about.

grille.name: steel grille
grille.text: A steel grille over the prize shelves. Behind it, bears, sunglasses and a radio-controlled car that has been the top prize for three years.

extra.text: It is rolled down and padlocked at the floor.

slush.name: slush machine
slush.text: A slush machine churning Blue Raspberry. The date on the hygiene sticker is from before you were hired.

ledger.name: pickup ledger
ledger.text: A pickup ledger: every delivery and collection, with a time and a signature.

register.name: register
register.text: An old cash register. Closed, and you were told on your first night never to touch it.

locker1.name: first locker
locker1.text: The first of three gray staff lockers, dented at knee height.

locker2.name: second locker
locker2.text: The middle of three gray staff lockers. Someone has stuck a Block Drop sticker on it.

locker3.name: third locker
locker3.text: The last of three gray staff lockers. Its door does not quite close.

officekey.name: brass key
officekey.text: A brass key on a hook ring, with OFFICE scratched into the bow.

desk.name: desk
desk.text: A steel desk under a lamp, covered in invoices. A framed photo stands at the corner.

safe.name: floor safe
safe.text: A squat floor safe under the desk with a four-digit combination dial.

extra.text: It is shut, and you would open it with the right four digits.
It stands open: the cash box, the deeds, and an empty hook where a ring of keys hung.

photo.name: framed photo
photo.text: Opening day, 1979: a younger Marge and a man in a wide tie cut a ribbon in front of the arcade. The frame is light, and something is written on the back of the print. You could turn it over.

panel.name: switch panel
panel.text: A panel of keyed switches, one per cabinet, each labeled with a game. Turned to EDIT, a switch lets whoever holds the key rewrite that cabinet's high score board. The Block Drop switch is turned to EDIT right now.

marge.name: Marge
marge.text: Marge Okafor, sixty, owner of the Starlight since opening day. Reading glasses, a cardigan, and a pencil she never puts down.

board.reply: "Nobody scores 999,999. Only the office panel can edit a board, and the panel key never leaves my ring." She touches the ring on her belt and frowns.

panel.reply: "Turned to EDIT? I never leave it on EDIT." She looks at the panel for a long moment and says nothing else.

safe.reply: "The safe is my business. You are the janitor."

photo.reply: "Opening day. That's Walt, my first partner. He's gone now, and so is his head for numbers."

night.reply: "Vacuum, mop, lock up. And now, apparently, find my cabinet."

galaxy.reply: "The Galaxy Patrol cabinet. Gone when I came down at one. ${witness} was in and out of here all evening, if you want somewhere to start."

pickup.reply: "Pickups go in the ledger. Nobody told me about a pickup tonight, and nobody signs my ledger at three in the morning with my say-so."

rudy.reply: "Rudy fixes the cabinets. He was in and out all evening with his toolbox, and he knows every one of those machines better than I do. He borrowed the Block Drop panel key last week to reset the board after a glitch. I'm sure he gave it back."

dale.reply: "Dale drives for the distributor. He brings the new cabinets in and takes the dead ones out. He was here after closing with the van, and the last I saw him he was heading for Lou's pie."

priya.reply: "Priya. Signs PRI. She has held the honest top score on that Block Drop for a year, and she does not take kindly to being pushed off it."

walt.reply: "Walt. My first partner. He kept the numbers in his head and then one day he didn't, so he started writing them down where he thought I'd never look."

token.reply: "Tokens are a dollar for four at the counter. Drop one in a cabinet and it plays, unless the machine's in service mode, in which case it tells you things it shouldn't."

key.reply: "The office key hangs in a staff locker so the night man can get in. The panel keys stay on my ring." She touches her belt again.

lockers.reply: "Staff lockers. Nothing in them worth stealing, which is why nobody locks them."

mop.reply: "The mop is for the floor. Also for reaching under things, if you're the type."

slush.reply: "Don't drink from that. I mean it."

grille.reply: "The prizes stay behind the grille until morning. The padlock key is on my ring, and the ring is on my belt."

register.reply: "The register is mine. You were told."

lou.reply: "Lou feeds the night shift. If anybody walked through that alley tonight, Lou saw them, and she will tell you if you ask nicely."

ring.reply: "That ring never leaves my belt, except at night, when it lives in the safe. Every panel key on it, and the padlock key for the grille." She does not look at the safe.

accuse.reply: "When you can put the key in my hand and tell me who had it, say the name. Not before. I don't accuse people on a hunch, and neither do you, not in my arcade."

marge.topicDefault: Marge looks at you over her glasses. "Is this about my cabinet? Then ask about that. Otherwise the floor needs you more than I do."

ring.name: ring of panel keys
ring.text: A steel ring of small keys, one per cabinet, each tagged with a game. The Block Drop tag is there; the key that belongs on it is not. A heavier brass padlock key hangs on the ring too.

fusebox.name: fuse box
fusebox.text: A fuse box with its door hanging open. Every breaker is on. Someone has written the cabinets' names on tape beside each one, and the Galaxy Patrol breaker has been switched off and taped over.

poster.name: Galaxy Patrol poster
poster.text: A faded poster for Galaxy Patrol, the arcade's first cabinet, from the year the place opened. Collectors pay real money for a working one now; there is a magazine clipping pinned to the corner that says so.

tube.name: fluorescent tube
tube.text: The tube flickers, steadies, and flickers again. It has done this since before you were hired.

dolly.name: hand dolly
dolly.text: A two-wheeled hand dolly, the kind for moving cabinets. The rubber on one wheel is fresh with sawdust.

clipboard.name: clipboard
clipboard.text: A clipboard hanging from a nail: the distributor's pickup slips, with a pouch on the back for whatever a driver does not want to carry.

fob.name: van key fob
fob.text: A black key fob with the distributor's logo, the kind that unlocks a van from across a lot.

lever.name: lift lever
lever.text: A steel lever in a box on the wall, for the dock's lift plate. The painted warning under it says STAND CLEAR, and the plate is the whole platform you are standing on.

tracks.name: tyre tracks
tracks.text: Fresh tyre tracks from the dock into the alley, with a pair of narrow wheel lines between them: a dolly, pushed, then loaded.

rollup.name: roll-up door
rollup.text: The roll-up door is all the way up. Nobody closed it after the pickup.

van.name: delivery van
van.text: A white delivery van with the distributor's name on the side, parked nose-out. The driver's seat is empty.

extra.text: The back doors are shut. Through the back window, the shape of moving blankets.
The back doors stand open on the cargo bay.

payphone.name: payphone
payphone.text: A payphone on the arcade's wall, its cord chewed by weather. The last-number redial button is worn shiny. It wants a quarter.

dumpster.name: dumpster
dumpster.text: A dumpster with its lid up, half full. A sign on the side says the truck comes at four.

stain.name: oil stain
stain.text: An oil stain on the asphalt in the shape of something that stood here on four feet for an hour and then was lifted into the van.

lamp.name: sodium lamp
lamp.text: The sodium lamp buzzes and makes everything the colour of weak tea.

bundle.name: wrapped cabinet
bundle.text: Under the blankets, the unmistakable shape of an upright cabinet, strapped tight. A corner of the marquee shows through: GALAXY PATROL.

label.name: shipping label
label.text: A shipping label taped to the strap, written in marker: HOLD FOR R.V. - COLLECTOR PICKUP 7 AM - PAID IN FULL. The distributor's own form, with the distributor's address crossed out.

blankets.name: moving blankets
blankets.text: Quilted moving blankets, the distributor's, thrown over something tall.

straps.name: straps
straps.text: Ratchet straps holding the bundle to the bulkhead, pulled by someone who knew how.

lou.name: Lou
lou.text: Lou has cooked the night shift at the Starlight Diner for longer than the arcade has had a Block Drop. She sees everything that walks past the window and remembers most of it.
lou.topicDefault: Lou taps her pencil on the crossword. "Ask me about the people, honey. The rest is just furniture."

dale.reply: "Dale? Been on that stool since one. Parked his van out back, came in for pie, put his head down. He hasn't moved, and I'd know, because his elbow's on my counter."

rudy.reply: "Rudy came in quarter past three. Hands black with solder, smelled like a hot iron. Didn't want pie, wanted change for the payphone. I gave him a quarter and he went straight back out to it."

phone.reply: "The payphone out back? Takes a quarter and remembers the last number it called, which is more than some people. I'm out of change. Try the floor; Dale's pockets leak."

van.reply: "Dale's van. He leaves the fob on his clipboard at your dock so Rudy can move it when there's a dead cabinet to collect. I told him that was a bad idea."

marge.reply: "Marge sends me the broken ones to feed. She's a good egg. She'd hate what's happening to her place tonight."

cabinet.reply: "Saw a cabinet go into that van around three, wrapped up like a Christmas present. Thought it was a pickup. Dale didn't do it; he was drooling on my counter."

priya.reply: "Priya came by for pie at eleven, like always, and went home. She'd never touch a machine she couldn't beat fair."

coffee.reply: "Coffee's a dollar, pie's two, and you look like you need both. On the house when you've found Marge's cabinet."

night.reply: "Night shift. Same as yours, except mine has pie."

dale.name: Dale
dale.text: Dale, the distributor's driver, asleep on the last stool with his head on his arms and his jacket collar up. He snores on the in-breath.
dale.topicDefault: Dale mumbles something into his sleeve and does not wake.

slips.reply: Without lifting his head: "Rudy keeps 'em... signed 'em blank for the dead ones... lemme sleep..."

van.reply: "Fob's on the clipboard... Rudy moves it... don't wake me..."

cabinet.reply: "No pickup tonight... told Marge... Tuesday..." He is asleep again before the word ends.

stool.name: stool
stool.text: A row of chrome stools. Dale has the last one. The floor under it is where things fall out of a sleeping man's pockets.

coffee.name: coffee
coffee.text: Two pots of coffee on their burners, one of them older than this shift.

piecase.name: pie case
piecase.text: A pie case with two slices of something cherry under the glass.

crossword.name: crossword
crossword.text: Lou's crossword, mostly done in ink. Fourteen across is CULPRIT.

bench.name: workbench
bench.text: A long workbench under a hanging lamp, scarred with solder burns. Screwdrivers, a magnifier, a coffee cup with a ring in it.

drawers.name: parts cabinet
drawers.text: A steel parts cabinet with three drawers: top, middle and bottom. Each has a strip of masking tape for a label: FUSES, SWITCHES, and one that just says BD. The BD tape is on the ${drawer.name}.

drawer1.name: top drawer
drawer1.text: The top drawer of the parts cabinet.

drawer2.name: middle drawer
drawer2.text: The middle drawer of the parts cabinet.

drawer3.name: bottom drawer
drawer3.text: The bottom drawer of the parts cabinet.

panelkey.name: Block Drop panel key
panelkey.text: A small brass key on a paper tag that reads BD in Marge's handwriting. It belongs on the ring in her safe.

monitor.name: monitor chassis
monitor.text: An arcade monitor out of its cabinet, lying open on the bench with its back off. The yellow sticker says the tube holds a charge for days after it is unplugged, and it is not unplugged.

iron.name: soldering iron
iron.text: A soldering iron in its stand, the tip still dark and warm. Somebody was using it within the hour.

toolbox.name: toolbox
toolbox.text: Rudy's red toolbox, open: wire cutters, a jigsaw blade with fresh sawdust on it, and a roll of the distributor's shipping labels.

backpanel.name: back panel
backpanel.text: The back panel of an arcade cabinet, sawn off with a jigsaw. Stencilled on the inside: GALAXY PATROL, and Marge's inventory tag, STARLIGHT 001. It never left the building whole. It left in pieces, and this piece did not fit in the van.

shelves.name: shelves
shelves.text: Steel shelves of plush animals in plastic bags, waiting for someone to win them.

cartons.name: cartons
cartons.text: Flattened cartons and a box of brass tokens, a dollar for four.

sawdust.name: sawdust
sawdust.text: Sawdust on the floor, on the shelves, in the plush. Someone used a jigsaw in here tonight.

rudy.name: Rudy
rudy.text: Rudy is not here. He went home around half past three, Lou says, after his phone call.

priya.name: Priya
priya.text: Priya is not here. She went home at eleven, with pie.

mat.name: dock mat
mat.text: A rubber mat at the top of the dock steps, cracked and curling at one corner.

envelope.name: envelope
envelope.text: A plain envelope, thick. Inside, used twenties, counted and banded. The price of a Galaxy Patrol cabinet, it turns out, is less than you would think and more than Rudy earns in a month.

do.reply: You get down on the carpet and look under the cabinet. Dust, a bottle cap, and a brass arcade token, which rolls out when you poke it with the mop handle.
Dust and a bottle cap. Nothing else under there.
The token drops. Instead of a game, the screen flips to a service page nobody was meant to see: LAST BOARD EDIT 03:07 FROM OFFICE PANEL. The cabinet keeps the token.
The token drops. Instead of a game, the screen flips to a service page nobody was meant to see: LAST BOARD EDIT 03:07 FROM OFFICE PANEL. The cabinet keeps the token.
The coin slot wants a token, and the attract screen wants an audience. You have neither.
The cabinet is stuck on its service page: LAST BOARD EDIT 03:07 FROM OFFICE PANEL.

do.die: You take hold of the frayed cord and pull. The split insulation finds your palm, the wall outlet finds the rest of you, and for one bright instant you are the best-lit thing in the Starlight. The attract screens never notice.
You grab the cord by the bare part. It is still plugged in. Your last thought is that someone should really have unplugged that.

do.reply: You nudge the cord aside with the mop handle. It sparks against the baseboard. Good instinct not to use your hand.
It is already the cleanest carpet in the building. That is rather the point.
The last line, in a hurried hand: 2:50 AM, PICKUP, 1 CABINET (GALAXY PATROL), and a signature that is mostly a loop. Two-fifty. Seventeen minutes before somebody typed ZZZ into the high score board.
The last line, in a hurried hand: 2:50 AM, PICKUP, 1 CABINET (GALAXY PATROL), and a signature that is mostly a loop. Two-fifty. Seventeen minutes before somebody typed ZZZ into the high score board.

do.die: You pull the lever and drink straight from the spout. The Blue Raspberry has been fermenting since Labor Day, and it has opinions. You sit down on the floor to think about them and do not get up.

do.reply: The locker opens with a squeal. A raincoat, a lunch box, and on a hook inside the door, a brass key.
The locker opens with a squeal. A raincoat, a lunch box, and on a hook inside the door, a brass key.
The locker opens with a squeal. A raincoat, a lunch box, and on a hook inside the door, a brass key.
A sock, a paperback with the cover torn off, and a smell. Nothing useful.
Empty but for a crumpled Starlight apron.
The door swings loose. Inside, a single boot.
The padlock at the floor disagrees.
You were told never to touch it. You don't.

rules.fail: You have nothing that fits that lock.

do.reply: The brass key turns. Unlocked. The office door swings open onto a desk lamp and a surprised silence. You are still on the floor; the office is north.
The brass key turns. Unlocked. The office door swings open onto a desk lamp and a surprised silence. You are still on the floor; the office is north.
The brass key turns. Unlocked. The office door swings open onto a desk lamp and a surprised silence. You are still on the floor; the office is north.
It's locked.
It is already open.
From inside, a pencil stops moving. Nobody answers.
You turn the frame over. On the back of the print, in pencil, in a hand that is not Marge's: ${combo}. Under it, smaller: DON'T FORGET AGAIN, WALT.
On the back of the print, in pencil, in a hand that is not Marge's: ${combo}. Under it, smaller: DON'T FORGET AGAIN, WALT.
Behind the print, in pencil: ${combo}. Under it, smaller: DON'T FORGET AGAIN, WALT.
Marge clears her throat. You put it back.
The switches need their little keys. Without one, they don't turn.
Marge is in the chair. She looks at you over her glasses until you stop.
You mop around the cord, carefully, as around something asleep.

You spin the dial to ${combo}. The safe clunks and swings open. Inside: the cash box, a stack of deeds, and the ring of little panel keys that never leaves Marge's belt. Except that it is here, and the Block Drop key is missing from it. Marge sees it at the same moment you do, and says nothing at all.

rules.fail: You try a number. The dial does not care for guesses, and neither does Marge, who is watching. Find the combination first.

Except that it is here, and the Block Drop key is missing from it. Marge sees it at the same moment you do, and says nothing at all.

Except that it is here, and the Block Drop key is missing from it. Marge sees it at the same moment you do, and says nothing at all.

rules.fail: You try a number. The dial does not care for guesses, and neither does Marge, who is watching. Find the combination first.

do.reply: The dial needs the right four-digit combination, and that was not it. Open the safe with the number, if you know it.
You spin the dial. It stops on nothing. It wants four particular digits, and it will not say which.
There is no keyhole, only a dial that wants four digits.
The office door is already unlocked and open.
Marge watches you lift her ring out of her safe and lets you. "Find the key that goes on it," she says. "Then we'll talk."

rules.fail: You need the padlock key for that, and it hangs on Marge's ring.

do.reply: The padlock key on Marge's ring turns the padlock. You roll the grille up far enough to duck under. The stockroom is in.
The padlock key on Marge's ring turns the padlock. You roll the grille up far enough to duck under. The stockroom is in.
The grille is already up. The stockroom is in.

Pickup slips, a pad of them, every one already signed at the bottom with the same loop that is in the ledger, and nothing else filled in. Dale signs them blank and leaves them here, and anyone with a pen can make a pickup official. The pouch on the back has something heavy in it.

Pickup slips, a pad of them, every one already signed at the bottom with the same loop that is in the ledger, and nothing else filled in. Dale signs them blank and leaves them here, and anyone with a pen can make a pickup official. The pouch on the back has something heavy in it.
In the pouch on the back of the clipboard: a black van key fob with the distributor's logo.
The pouch is empty now.

do.die: You pull the lift lever. The warning said STAND CLEAR, and the lift plate is the platform you are standing on. It drops four feet in a quarter of a second and you do not drop with it so much as after it. The caged bulb swings. Somewhere a van door is still open.

You push the lift lever. The warning said STAND CLEAR, and the lift plate is the platform you are standing on. It drops four feet in a quarter of a second and you do not drop with it so much as after it. The caged bulb swings.

do.reply: You pull the roll-up door down a foot and it jams. It was never going to be that easy.

rules.fail: The van is locked, and you have nothing that opens it.

do.reply: You press the fob. The van chirps and its back doors unlock. You swing them open on a cargo bay that smells of rubber and cold coffee.
You press the fob. The van chirps and its back doors unlock. You swing them open on a cargo bay that smells of rubber and cold coffee.
You press the fob. The van chirps and its back doors unlock. You swing them open on a cargo bay that smells of rubber and cold coffee.
Locked. The back doors do not budge, and the driver's door is locked too.

do.die: You climb into the dumpster to see what somebody threw away tonight. The lid comes down. The sign said the truck comes at four, and the truck is punctual. The last thing you hear is the hydraulics.
You climb into the dumpster to see what somebody threw away tonight. The lid comes down. The sign said the truck comes at four, and the truck is punctual. The last thing you hear is the hydraulics.

do.reply: You lean over the edge: cardboard, a broken joystick, pie boxes from the diner. Nothing you would climb in for.
The quarter drops and the payphone gives you a dial tone and the smell of a hundred strangers' breath. The redial button is worn shiny. Press it.
The quarter drops and the payphone gives you a dial tone and the smell of a hundred strangers' breath. The redial button is worn shiny. Press it.

rules.fail: The payphone wants a quarter before it will do anything, including remember.

do.reply: You press redial. Two rings, then an answering machine with a slow, pleased voice: "You've reached Vance Amusements, buying and restoring classic cabinets. Rudy, if that's you again: the Galaxy Patrol money is in the envelope under the dock mat like we said, and I'll be by at seven with the truck. Pleasure doing business." You hang up very carefully.

Rudy, if that's you again: the Galaxy Patrol money is in the envelope under the dock mat like we said, and I'll be by at seven with the truck. Pleasure doing business." You hang up very carefully.
You look under Dale's stool. Pocket lint, a bottle cap, and a quarter, heads up.
Lint and a bottle cap. That is all Dale had.
You shake Dale's shoulder. He says "Tuesday," clearly, and goes on sleeping. Lou shakes her head at you.
Lou pours you a cup without being asked. It is terrible and you are grateful.
"After," Lou says, without looking up from the crossword.
The top drawer slides out. Under a nest of fuses, a small brass key on a paper tag that says BD, in Marge's handwriting.
The middle drawer slides out. Under a nest of fuses, a small brass key on a paper tag that says BD, in Marge's handwriting.
The bottom drawer slides out. Under a nest of fuses, a small brass key on a paper tag that says BD, in Marge's handwriting.
Fuses, hundreds of them, sorted by amperage with a care that borders on love.
Microswitches and joystick springs, loose, rattling.
Coin mechs, a dozen of them, and a paperback about fishing.

do.die: You reach into the open monitor chassis. The sticker said the tube holds a charge for days. It holds it for exactly as long as it takes to find your hand, and then it gives it all to you at once. The bench lamp swings. The soldering iron, patient, stays warm.

do.reply: Warm. Used within the hour, by someone with a lot of soldering to do, or a lot of solder to get on his hands.
It is plugged in and it is not yours. You leave it.
Marge takes her glasses off. "Me? I own the place. Try again, and try harder."

do.win: "Rudy," Marge says, and it is not a question. She takes the panel key from your hand, looks at the BD tag in her own writing, and puts it back on the ring where it belongs. Then she picks up the office phone and dials three digits. By the time the sun comes up over the Starlight the police have the van, the collector has a very bad morning ahead, and Rudy, who came in early to put a key back, finds Marge waiting. She does not raise her voice. She never has to. "You," she says to you, when it is over, "did good. The floor still needs vacuuming."

rules.fail: Dale snores. Accusing a sleeping man gets you nowhere; say it to Marge, in the office.

do.reply: "Dale?" Marge looks at you. "Dale has been asleep on Lou's counter since one, and Lou would know. Think again."
"Priya? She holds the honest score on that machine. She'd sooner burn the place down than cheat it. No."
Lou laughs so hard she has to put the crossword down.
It is already open.

The lid is already up.
The safe is already open.
It is already all the way up.
It is heavier than it looks and it stays where Rudy left it.
You shift the cartons. Sawdust, and more sawdust.
Marge waits. "A hunch is not proof. Bring me the key that is missing from my ring, and then say the name."
Marge turns the panel key over in her fingers. "You have the key. Now tell me who had it. Something that says so, not a hunch."
Say it to Marge, in the office. Accusations need a witness.
You lift the corner of the mat. An envelope, thick, exactly where a voice on an answering machine said it would be.
Nothing under the mat now but the shape of the envelope in the dust.
Taken. It is evidence now, and it is heavy in your pocket in more ways than one.
